page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-8 is an entry-tier virtual machine within the Standard instance family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor with a base clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. The instance is allocated 1 physical core configured with two hardware threads, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile suitable for general-purpose application execution.

The hardware configuration includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and omits local storage disks entirely, necessitating the use of remote block storage services for root filesystems and persistent application data. Similarly, the instance contains zero GPUs or dedicated hardware coprocessors. Because the vCPUs are assigned dedicated core resources rather than burstable or shared allocations, the execution environment avoids noisy-neighbor contention for underlying CPU cycles.

Given its minimal core count and standard memory-to-core allocation, VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-8 is suitable for baseline infrastructure tasks. Common workload applications include lightweight web serving, application routing, small-scale API endpoints, testing or continuous integration workers, and containerized microservices operating under modest concurrency demands.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-8 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Standard family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor based on the x86_64 architecture running at 3.9 GHz, it provides 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of memory, delivering an industry-standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. There is no local storage included, necessitating remote block storage solutions for persistent data needs, nor does it include GPU accelerators. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated core allocation and compact footprint, the instance offers predictable execution efficiency for modest workloads. VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-8 is suited for utility workloads such as lightweight web and application serving, continuous integration nodes, staging environments, and basic microservice hosting.
